3-PG is the dominant phosphoglycerate pool and Li et al. assigned the feature with a 3-PG standard. 2-PG is isobaric and may co-elute, but PGAM1 (interconverts 3-PG and 2-PG) is already in the gene set, so the set covers the sum of both species.
'alpha' names the 1/3 isomer; glycerol 2-phosphate is a minor cellular species. Mapped to sn-glycerol 3-phosphate (MAM02914).

Sorbitol (AKR1B1/SORD polyol pathway) is the hexitol human cells make; mannitol is not synthesised by human cells. Caveat: the 12 primary lines in Leibovitz L-15 are grown on galactose, where galactitol (AKR1B1 product, isobaric) is possible.

Lactose is synthesised only by lactating mammary epithelium (LALBA/B4GALT1); an intracellular signal in cancer lines more plausibly reflects FBS carry-over or an unresolved isobaric disaccharide. A first-neighbour gene set for lactose is not biologically meaningful here.
5-oxoproline forms non-enzymatically and in the ion source by cyclisation of glutamine and glutamate, so the measured signal is partly an artefact of much larger pools.
